text:
Maya: Quick spike outcome: we profiled a small model family with interpolated quant profiles (mixing FP8 for attn, INT8 for MLP), results surprising. want to sync on handshake rules.
Jon: Short version: mixing formats gives good perf but weird tail effects on long prompts. sometimes last-token confidence drops.
Tara: Can you paste the numbers?
Maya: Sure, high level:
- FP8-attn + INT8-mlp: 22% cost reduction, median latency -12ms, but p99 increased ~9% on 2/50 test cases.
- FP8 everywhere: 28% cost reduction, p99 +2%
- INT8 everywhere: 15% cost reduction, p99 stable.
Jon: So hybrid wins on cost but risks spikes. We need a runtime contract: allow hybrid only for endpoints with short-tail SLAs or with enforced cache invalidation.
Tara: Proposal: categorize endpoints by ctx_length_profile and user_impact_score. Hybrid allowed if ctx_profile = short AND impact_score < 0.3.
Leo: Also runtime interface: when applying an interpolated profile we must emit a quant-profile-id header and a cache-stamp. If KV cache binary layout changes, invalidate.
Maya: Agreed. Also observed an operational quirk: when fallback from FP8->INT8 occurred mid-request (rare), cached activations mismatched and produced garbled token. Need atomic switch semantics.
Jon: Atomic switch semantics = drain in-flight requests for affected workers OR operate per-request routing where new requests go to new bin and old requests finish on old.
Tara: Drain approach could spike latency. Per-request routing needs compatibility checks for cache keys. Maybe we support both via a switch_mode flag.
Leo: Can we add a lightweight compatibility header: quant_binary_hash + kv_schema_version. Controller checks and if mismatch it sets route.invalidate_kv=true.
ops-bot: canary status for model-alpha: probe_window=1000, last_window_samples=1200, hybrid_success=78%, p99_latency_delta=0.09, breakdown: FP8-attn_OK=85%, INT8-mlp_OK=90%
Maya: ops-bot suggests p99 delta 9% which is borderline for many routes. We should fail fast for high-impact routes.
Jon: Also add a gradual ramp: start with 5% traffic, monitor topk-token-shifts and deg_score. doubling every 30min until either threshold or 100%.
Tara: Agreed. thresholds: deg_score delta < 1% AND topk_shift_rate < 3%. Also require no customer error rate increase.
Leo: For observability add per-worker quant-profile telemetry: applied_profile, binary_hash, kv_stamp, last_switch_ts, in_flight_count. Helpful for triage.
Maya: One more: for per-layer fallbacks, provide a deterministic fallback map in the profile (e.g., layer 0..3 -> FP8, 4..23 -> INT8) so runtime doesn't guess.
Jon: +1. Determinism also helps golden replays and evals.
Tara: Action items:
- Jon: write runtime switch_mode RFC (drain vs per-request)
- Leo: add headers and kv_stamp to promote API + telemetry
- Maya: run 24h hybrid canary with ramping schedule and collect degscore + topk histograms
- Tara: update per-route policy docs (which endpoints allowed)

Maya: I'll post the raw trace artifacts and replay harness link shortly.
Jon: I'll grab a seat for a quick design review tomorrow.
Tara: thanks all :rocket:
